brief: Goldman's midday desk note reports US indices lower with the macro picture in focus. WTI breaks $100 for the first time since late May and the US 10 year yield hits 4.90%, the highest since November 2023, with September hike estimates at 70%. NDX is down 71bps on a fourth straight down day and SPX down 40bps, testing its 50 day moving average at 7603, while a 26th consecutive session of sub 1% intraday ranges marks the longest such streak in five years. High beta momentum, memory and semis lead the downside, megacap tech is unchanged, defense gains 136bps on Middle East escalation, and the copper basket falls 550bps after a Reuters report that the US is delaying copper tariffs over inflation concerns. August core PPI came in below expectations, but PCE relevant components lifted the estimated monthly core PCE to 0.24%. The desk forecasts 0.23% core CPI against 0.2% consensus. The floor is 9% better for sale on quiet activity, long only and hedge fund flows both skew to sell, and short term CTA thresholds across NDX, SPX and RTY broke this morning.
